title: Flood Warning
description: ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida... St Johns River Near Deland affecting Lake and Volusia Counties. .Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns at Deland to reach Major Flood Stage. The river is forecast to continue a gradual rise through the week, and may approach its record flood. For the St. Johns River...including Deland...Major flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast. * WHERE...St Johns River near Deland. * WHEN...Until further notice. * IMPACTS...At 5.3 feet, Major flooding occurs to many structures and marinas along the river and in the Hontoon Island area. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 8:30 PM EST Sunday the stage was 5.4 feet. - Bankfull stage is 3.5 feet. - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 8:30 PM EST Sunday was 5.4 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 6.1 feet late this week. Additional rises are possible thereafter. - Flood stage is 4.0 feet. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

title: Flood Warning
description: ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida... St Johns River Near Above Lake Harney affecting Seminole County. .Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns Above Lake Harney near Geneva to remain within Major Flood Stage. River levels are forecast to reach a crest tonight before beginning a very slow decline within Major flood stage later in the week. For the St. Johns River...including Above Lake Harney...Major flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast. The river has surpassed its previous record flood. * WHERE...St Johns River near Above Lake Harney. * WHEN...Until further notice. * IMPACTS...At 10.8 feet, Water covers State Road 46 and it may become impassable near Jungle Road and Prevatt Road. Standing water on secondary roads near the river deepens to more than three feet in some areas. Flooding becomes more significant to structures and marinas from above Lake Harney to the Lake Jesup area. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 7:30 AM EST Sunday the stage was 12.8 feet. - Bankfull stage is 6.0 feet. - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 7:30 AM EST Sunday was 12.8 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 13.1 feet tonight. The river is then forecast to begin a slow decline through this week. - Flood stage is 8.0 feet. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
